facts.fact: Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, Microsoft Agent 365 and Copilot Studio subscriptions are all hosted in a Microsoft Entra tenant (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-365-overview)
Agent management happens in the Microsoft 365 admin center (`admin.microsoft.com` / `admin.cloud.microsoft`) under Agents (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-365-overview)
The Microsoft 365 admin center is at `admin.microsoft.com` / `admin.cloud.microsoft`, with agent management under Agents (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-365-overview)

The Power Platform hierarchy is tenant > environment group > environment > (optional) Dataverse database, and the roles you assign differ depending on whether an environment has a Dataverse database (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/database-security)
A Power Platform environment can have zero or one Dataverse database (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/database-security)
Power Platform environment groups are folders of Managed Environments only (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/environment-groups)

Each environment belongs to at most one environment group, groups can't be nested, and group rules lock the matching settings in member environments (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/environment-groups)

Microsoft 365 Copilot is an add-on that needs a qualifying base license; eligible commercial bases include Microsoft 365 E3/E5/F1/F3, Business Basic/Standard/Premium, Office 365 E1/E3/E5/F3, plus some Teams, Exchange and SharePoint plans (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/copilot-license-options)
Microsoft 365 E7 includes Copilot, so no separate qualifying base plus add-on is needed there (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/copilot-license-options)
Microsoft Copilot Business is the SMB variant, capped at 300 users per tenant (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/copilot-license-options)

Microsoft Copilot Business is an annual-commitment add-on for eligible Microsoft 365 Business plans and has the same Copilot capabilities (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/copilot-license-options)
Copilot is available in US Government clouds as an add-on in GCC, GCC High and DoD for G5/G3/F1 and related plans (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/copilot-license-options)
Copilot Studio needs a tenant license listed as 'Copilot Studio' (a prepaid Copilot Credit pack) (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-licensing)

Copilot Studio makers need the 'Copilot Studio User License', which is free and assignable only after a tenant pack exists (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-licensing)

Both the Copilot Studio tenant license and the Copilot Studio User License are bought in Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Purchase services, or both through the same volume-licensing channel (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-licensing)

A maker can also get Copilot Studio access through the Power Platform admin center 'Copilot Studio authors' security-group setting, a Microsoft 365 Copilot license (Microsoft Copilot harness agents), or a trial license (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/billing-licensing)
Copilot Studio trial users can build and test agents but can't publish them (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/billing-licensing)
Guest users can't access Copilot Studio; users of a published agent need no special license to chat with it (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-licensing)
Admins can set the Entra `AllowAdHocSubscriptions` flag to stop users signing up for Copilot Studio trials themselves (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-licensing)
Agent 365 is GA for the Commercial segment, licensed per user, and needs at least one licensed user (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/overview)
Microsoft 365 E5 is the recommended prerequisite for Agent 365 (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/overview)

Day-one asks for an engineer joining a client: (1) a licensed work account in the client tenant with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license plus a Copilot Studio User License or Copilot Studio authors membership; (2) the Environment Maker Dataverse role, or System Customizer to create tables, in a non-default dev environment; (3) an Entra app registration, or permission to request admin consent, for Graph access; (4) confirmation of who holds AI Administrator, Power Platform Administrator and Billing Administrator (secondary: synthesis of the cited pages) (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-share-bots ; https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-roles-perms)

An engineer building in Copilot Studio should get the Environment Maker Dataverse role in a non-default dev environment, or System Customizer if they must create tables (secondary: synthesis of the cited pages) (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-share-bots)

Agent approval is held by the AI Administrator, while Power Platform Administrator covers environments, data policies and capacity and Billing Administrator covers Copilot Credits (secondary: synthesis of the cited pages) (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-roles-perms)

Graph access for a joining engineer needs an Entra app registration, or permission to request admin consent (secondary: synthesis of the cited pages) (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-roles-perms)

The Copilot extensibility docs entry point https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-copilot/extensibility/ resolves and is titled 'Extending Microsoft 365 Copilot with plugins' (updated 2026-11-05) (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-copilot/extensibility/)
The Copilot extensibility landing page now centres on Work IQ Dev Tools (`wiqd`) and plugins (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-copilot/extensibility/)

The Copilot Studio docs root https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/ (updated 2026-11-12) groups content under Microsoft Copilot harness, Customer Conversation harness (preview) and standard harness (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/)
The Microsoft Copilot harness is one of the harnesses the Copilot Studio docs are organised by (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/)
The Customer Conversation harness is labelled preview on the Copilot Studio docs root updated 2026-11-12 (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/)
The standard harness is one of the harnesses the Copilot Studio docs are organised by (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/)

facts.fact: The Power Platform docs root https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/ (updated 2026-10-26) resolves (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/)
The Graph docs root https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/ loads and links to the API changelog `https://developer.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/changelog` (https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/)
The Graph docs hub links to the Microsoft MCP Server for Enterprise (https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/)
The Agent 365 docs root is https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/overview, updated 2026-11-11 (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/overview)

Microsoft Entra Agent ID is a dedicated identity type for AI agents, available to all Entra customers, with four objects: `agentIdentityBlueprint` (template that holds credentials), `agentIdentityBlueprintPrincipal` (the blueprint's record in a tenant), `agentIdentity` (primary runtime identity, no credentials of its own) and the optional `agentUser` (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/agent-id/key-concepts ; https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/agentid-platform-overview?view=graph-rest-beta)
`agentIdentityBlueprint` is the Entra Agent ID template object that holds credentials (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/agent-id/key-concepts)
The optional `agentUser` is a 1:1 user account for an agent, for systems that require a user object (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/agent-id/key-concepts)
Agent identities get tokens through their blueprint, which holds the credentials and acquires tokens for every agent identity created from it (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/agent-id/key-concepts)
Conditional Access applied to an agent identity blueprint applies to all its agent identities (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/agent-id/key-concepts)
Interactive agents act for a signed-in user with delegated permissions through the on-behalf-of (OBO) flow (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/agent-id/key-concepts)
Autonomous agents use their own agent identity with the client credentials flow (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/agent-id/key-concepts)

Microsoft advises against service principals and user accounts for AI agents because traditional service principals lack enforced sponsorship, agent-aware audit entries and blueprint-managed lifecycle, and human user accounts break Conditional Access and ID Protection (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/agent-id/key-concepts)

Copilot Studio agents get an Entra agent identity on creation; the creating user is recorded as sponsor and the agent's sign-ins are logged in Entra as AI-agent activity (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/agent-id/what-are-agent-identities)
Extending Entra security features to agents requires Agent 365 (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/agent-id/what-are-agent-identities)
Agent 365 is included in Microsoft 365 E7, or is an add-on to E5, A5, Business Premium, or Defender Suite plus Purview Suite (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/agent-id/what-are-agent-identities)

Agent identities carry owners (technical admins), sponsors (business accountability) and managers (for `agentUser`), and entitlement management, access reviews and lifecycle workflows extend to them (https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/agentid-platform-overview?view=graph-rest-beta)

Agent identities can't be granted many high-risk Graph application permissions, including `Files.Read.All`, `Sites.Read.All`, `Sites.ReadWrite.All`, `Chat.Read.All`, `Calendars.Read`, `Application.ReadWrite.All`, `Directory.ReadWrite.All`, `User.ReadWrite.All` and `RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory`; requesting one returns HTTP `400 Bad Request` (https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/agentid-platform-overview?view=graph-rest-beta ; https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/permissions-overview)

The old Entra Agent Registry Graph APIs `agentRegistry`, `agentCardManifest`, `agentInstance` and `agentCollection` are deprecated (https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/agentid-platform-overview?view=graph-rest-beta)

Starting May 2026, Agent Registry APIs powered by Microsoft Agent 365 are replacing `agentRegistry`, `agentCardManifest`, `agentInstance` and `agentCollection` (https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/agentid-platform-overview?view=graph-rest-beta)

Copilot Studio end-user authentication has three options: `No authentication`, `Authenticate with Microsoft` and `Authenticate manually` (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication)

`Authenticate with Microsoft` gives automatic Entra SSO in Teams, SharePoint, Power Apps and Microsoft Copilot, but provides no `User.AccessToken` (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication)

`Authenticate manually` providers are Entra ID V2 with federated credentials, with certificates (Key Vault URL), or with client secrets, Entra ID, and generic OAuth 2 (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication)

The built-in 'Teams + Microsoft 365' channel requires `Authenticate with Microsoft`; manual authentication in Teams needs separate SSO and app manifest configuration (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication)

A Dataverse application user is the machine identity for Power Platform data access: an unlicensed Dataverse user bound to one Entra app registration, or to an Azure Managed Identity application ID, given Dataverse security roles (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/manage-application-users)

Application users are created in Power Platform admin center > Environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Application users (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/manage-application-users)
The limit is one Dataverse application user per Entra app per environment (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/manage-application-users)

Dataverse application users are created and assigned security roles in the Power Platform admin center under Environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Application users (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/manage-application-users)

facts.fact: Application users aren't blocked by environment security groups; they can run in environments secured with a security group without being a member (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/manage-application-users)

`pac admin create-service-principal --environment <id>` creates the Entra app and registers it with Power Platform (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/powerplatform-api-create-service-principal)

A service principal can't register itself; an admin with user context must register it through `PUT https://api.bap.microsoft.com/providers/Microsoft.BusinessAppPlatform/adminApplications/{clientId}` (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/powerplatform-api-create-service-principal)

Admin application registration uses `PUT https://api.bap.microsoft.com/providers/Microsoft.BusinessAppPlatform/adminApplications/{clientId}` (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/powerplatform-api-create-service-principal)

Once registered, a Power Platform API SPN is treated like a user with the Power Platform Administrator role (tenant-admin-level power), and granular roles can't be applied (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/powerplatform-api-create-service-principal)

Shared Copilot Studio agents with user-scoped connections need a strategy because connections are tied to each agent user's identity; Microsoft recommends a service principal where supported, environment-level connections, or per-user OAuth sign-in (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-share-bots)
Graph delegated permissions (scopes) are bounded by the signed-in user's own access (https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/permissions-overview)
Graph application permissions (app roles) reach all data the permission covers and need admin consent (https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/permissions-overview)

facts.target: Microsoft Entra Privileged Role Administrator role
facts.fact: Only Privileged Role Administrator and Global Administrator can consent to Graph application permissions (https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/permissions-overview)
Global Administrator is one of only two roles (with Privileged Role Administrator) that can consent to Graph application permissions (https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/permissions-overview)

Graph connector agents need application permissions with tenant-wide admin consent; delegated permissions aren't supported for connector agent registration (https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/permissions-overview)
Microsoft 365 Copilot surfaces only data the individual user can at least view (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/microsoft-365-copilot-privacy)
Semantic Index honours the user-identity access boundary for Microsoft 365 Copilot (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/microsoft-365-copilot-privacy)

AI Administrator is the main Entra role for Copilot and agent governance, template ID `d2562ede-74db-457e-a7b6-544e236ebb61`, privileged (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference)

AI Administrator manages all aspects of Microsoft Copilot, Integrated apps and Copilot agents, admin consent request policies and approving/publishing line-of-business agents (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference)
AI Administrator also covers the full lifecycle of agent identities, blueprints and agent users (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference)

facts.fact: Agent ID Administrator (template ID `db506228-d27e-4b7d-95e5-295956d6615f`, privileged) manages agent identity objects tenant-wide, covering lifecycle operations for blueprints, blueprint principals, agent identities and agent users (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference)

facts.source: Microsoft Entra Agent ID Developer role
facts.fact: Agent ID Developer (template ID `adb2368d-a9be-41b5-8667-d96778e081b0`) creates agent identity blueprints; creating a blueprint and its principal adds the user as owner of both (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference)

Only Global Administrator and AI Administrator can act on agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center: approving requests, assigning owners, installing and modifying agents (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-roles-perms)

Global Administrator is one of the two roles (with AI Administrator) that can approve requests, assign owners, install and modify agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-roles-perms)

Global Reader and AI Reader are read-only for agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center; Security Administrator/Reader, Reports Reader and User Experience Success Manager can only view (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-roles-perms)
AI Reader is read-only for agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-roles-perms)

Product admin roles only govern inside their own product: Power Platform Administrator and Fabric Administrator are scoped to their products, while AI Administrator and Global Administrator have tenant-wide agent authority (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-roles-perms)
Fabric Administrator is scoped to Fabric and has no tenant-wide agent authority (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-roles-perms)
Pinning agents for users in Microsoft Copilot requires the AI Administrator role (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-registry-overview)
Admins can pin up to three agents per user in Microsoft Copilot, and pins can take up to six hours to appear (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-registry-overview)

Power Platform Administrator (template ID `11648597-926c-4cf3-9c36-bcebb0ba8dcc`) manages all environments, ignores environment security groups, and can view and manage tenant and environment data policies (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/use-service-admin-role-manage-tenant ; https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference)
Power Platform Administrator can't create users or assign licenses (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/use-service-admin-role-manage-tenant)

Unlike Power Platform Administrator, Dynamics 365 Administrator is bound by environment security groups and must be a member of an environment's security group to manage that environment (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/use-service-admin-role-manage-tenant)

facts.fact: Global Administrator, Power Platform Administrator and Dynamics 365 Administrator must be assigned directly (they can't be inherited through security groups) and no longer auto-receive System Administrator in environments (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/use-service-admin-role-manage-tenant ; https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/database-security)

Power Platform Administrator doesn't grant Dataverse data access; admins self-elevate, or use Entra PIM, to get the Dataverse System Administrator role (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/use-service-admin-role-manage-tenant)

Dynamics 365 Administrator can't be inherited through security groups and no longer auto-receives System Administrator in environments (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/use-service-admin-role-manage-tenant)
Tenant admins get the Dataverse System Administrator role by self-elevating or through Entra PIM (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/database-security)
Environments without Dataverse have only two predefined roles: Environment Admin and Environment Maker (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/database-security)

Environment Admin handles all admin actions in an environment without Dataverse: adding users, provisioning Dataverse and creating data policies (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/database-security)
Environment Maker creates apps, connections, custom APIs and flows, with no data access (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/database-security)

Predefined Dataverse security roles can't be edited; they include App Opener, Basic User, Delegate, Environment Maker, Service Reader, Service Writer, Support User, System Administrator and System Customizer (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/database-security)
Makers who create or modify Dataverse tables need System Customizer in addition to Environment Maker (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/database-security)
Authoring desktop flows needs System Customizer or System Administrator; Environment Maker can't author them (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/database-security)
Authoring AI Builder needs System Customizer or System Administrator; Environment Maker can't author it (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/database-security)

Copilot Studio co-authors need the Environment Maker Dataverse role; if they lack it, the sharer must be a System Administrator so Copilot Studio can assign it (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-share-bots)
Chatting with a Copilot Studio agent requires the `ChatBotReaders` privilege, which Environment Maker includes (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-share-bots)

Copilot Studio transcript access needs the Bot Transcript Viewer Dataverse role; only admins have it by default, and it grants transcripts for all agents a user creates or is shared in that environment (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-share-bots)
The per-agent Copilot Studio sharing roles are Analytics Viewer and Agent viewer (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-share-bots)
Agent viewer is a per-agent Copilot Studio sharing role alongside Analytics Viewer (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-share-bots)

Sharing a Copilot Studio agent for chat with users or security groups works only when the agent uses `Authenticate manually` with Entra ID and 'Require users to sign in' is on (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-share-bots)
Microsoft 365 groups with `SecurityEnabled=false` can't be Copilot Studio chat sharing targets (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-share-bots)
Power Platform tenant isolation is set by a Power Platform Administrator (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/cross-tenant-restrictions)

Global Administrator and Billing Administrator can add and change Copilot Credits billing methods in the Microsoft 365 admin center Copilot > Cost Management (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-setup)

Billing Administrator can add and change Copilot Credits billing methods in Microsoft 365 admin center Copilot > Cost Management (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-setup)

AI Administrator and License Administrator can edit Copilot Credits spending policies, limits and alerts but can't create policies; AI Reader and Global Reader are view-only (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-setup)
License Administrator can edit Copilot Credits spending policies, limits and alerts but can't create policies (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-setup)

For least privilege, an agent calling Graph should prefer delegated (OBO) permissions with the narrowest scope (for example `User.Read`, `Calendars.ReadWrite` only if writing), and use application permissions only for background agents with a constraint such as `Selected` or `OwnedBy` (secondary: synthesis) (https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/permissions-overview ; https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/agentid-platform-overview?view=graph-rest-beta)

For Entra agent identities, broad permissions like `Sites.Read.All` and `Files.Read.All` are blocked (secondary: synthesis) (https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/agentid-platform-overview?view=graph-rest-beta)
Agent Registry, the tenant-wide agent inventory, is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > Registry (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-registry-overview)

Agent Registry publisher types are Microsoft agents, External partner-built agents, Published by your org (LOB) and Shared by creator, and the same Copilot Studio agent can appear under several (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-registry-overview)

Org-wide agents require admin approval in Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > Requests; agents from Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry or Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit are submitted as Pending review, Pending update or Pending activate, and admins choose Publish to store (pick users or groups, policy template, grant admin consent for requested permissions) or Reject submission (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-requests)

Admins can enable, block, remove and assign agents; users only see agents the admin allows and they've installed or been assigned, and the Integrated apps view shows each agent's permissions, terms and privacy statement (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/manage-copilot-agents-integrated-apps ; https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/microsoft-365-copilot-privacy)

facts.fact: With unified agent and app management, org-wide agent and app settings sync between the Microsoft 365 admin center and the Teams admin center (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-registry-overview)

Agent Registry is programmable through Graph (preview) via `GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/copilot/admin/catalog/packages` and package details (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-registry-overview)
The Agent Registry Graph endpoints need permission `CopilotPackages.Read.All` (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-registry-overview)
Calling the Agent Registry Graph endpoints needs the AI Administrator role (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-registry-overview)
Agent Registry programmability through Graph is in preview as of 2026-11-14 (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-registry-overview)
Agent risk signals require an E7 or Agent 365 license (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-registry-overview)
Agent risk signals aggregate Defender, Entra and Purview signals and can lag the security portals by up to an hour (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-registry-overview)
Opening Purview IRM alerts needs the IRM Analyst or IRM Investigator role; Global Administrator alone isn't enough (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/admin/agent-registry-overview)

Agent 365 GA scope (2026-05-01) covers observability, governance and security for delegated and own-credential agents, plus Entra network controls for Copilot Studio agents and endpoint agents (https://www.microsoft.com/security/blog/2026/05/01/microsoft-agent-365-now-generally-available-expands-capabilities-and-integrations/)

Still in preview in Agent 365: registry sync with AWS Bedrock and Google Cloud, Windows 365 for Agents (US only) and Defender/Intune local agent discovery (planned June 2026) (https://www.microsoft.com/security/blog/2026/05/01/microsoft-agent-365-now-generally-available-expands-capabilities-and-integrations/)

Windows 365 for Agents is in preview and US only as of the Agent 365 GA announcement (https://www.microsoft.com/security/blog/2026/05/01/microsoft-agent-365-now-generally-available-expands-capabilities-and-integrations/)
Power Platform 'data loss prevention' policies are now titled 'Data policies' (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/wp-data-loss-prevention)

Data policies are the connector guardrail governing Power Apps, Power Automate and Copilot Studio connectors at tenant or environment scope (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/wp-data-loss-prevention)

Data policy enforcement can take up to 24 hours (usually within an hour), and violating apps, flows and agents are suspended and their connections disabled (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/wp-data-loss-prevention)

Copilot Studio features are governed by virtual connectors in data policies covering maker and user auth, knowledge sources, actions, HTTP, channels, Application Insights and triggers (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/wp-data-loss-prevention ; https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/security-and-governance)
Advanced connector policies (ACP) don't support virtual connectors (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/wp-data-loss-prevention)

Copilot Studio virtual connectors are becoming dedicated governance rules, and Desktop Flow virtual connectors are becoming certified connectors (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/security-and-governance)

MCP servers can be restricted through advanced connector policies; MCP connectors expose MCP tools from connectors, and blocked MCP servers fail at runtime (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/wp-data-loss-prevention)

Managed Environments unlock environment groups, sharing limits, usage insights, desktop-flow data policies, IP Firewall, IP cookie binding, customer-managed key, Lockbox, extended backup, pipelines, default environment routing, VNet support and masking rules (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/managed-environment-overview)

The Managed Environments entitlement comes with standalone Power Apps, Power Automate, Copilot Studio, Power Pages and Dynamics 365 licenses (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/managed-environment-overview)
The Developer Plan does not carry the Managed Environments entitlement (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/managed-environment-overview)

Unmanaged developer environments are deprecated: creation ends 2026-11-15, suspension 2026-12-15 and deletion 2027-01-15; enable Managed Environments before 2026-12-15 to keep one (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/important-changes-coming ; https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/managed-environment-overview)

Dataverse for Teams environments are being retired: creation ends 2026-11-15, suspension 2027-09-15 and decommission 2027-10-30 unless upgraded (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/important-changes-coming)

Tenant isolation blocks inbound and outbound cross-tenant connections for Entra-authenticated connectors in canvas apps and Power Automate flows (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/cross-tenant-restrictions)

Configure tenant isolation at Power Platform admin center > Security > Identity and access > Tenant isolation, with allowlist rules by tenant ID or domain (max 500, `*` wildcard); changes take about an hour to apply (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/cross-tenant-restrictions)
The Azure DevOps connector isn't enforced by Power Platform tenant isolation (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/cross-tenant-restrictions)

Power Platform VNet support uses Azure subnet delegation for private outbound calls and is GA for Dataverse plug-ins and for SQL Server, Azure Key Vault, Blob, Files, Queues, custom connectors, HTTP with Entra ID, Snowflake, Databricks and Azure AI Search (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/vnet-support-overview)

VNet support requires a Managed Environment, a linked Azure subscription and VNets in both paired Azure regions; trial and Dataverse for Teams environments aren't supported (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/vnet-support-overview)

facts.fact: Copilot Studio governance controls include customer-managed keys, Customer Lockbox, environment routing, maker welcome message, an automatic security scan before publishing and a tenant switch to disable publishing of generative-AI agents (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/security-and-governance)
Copilot Studio Customer Lockbox doesn't cover Purview audit telemetry or Agent 365 governance events (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/security-and-governance)

Copilot Studio agents can be governed as Entra identities through Agent 365, with Conditional Access, RBAC/ABAC and access governance; Entra network egress and ingress controls for these agents are GA (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/security-and-governance)

Copilot Studio content moderation covers predefined harmful-content categories, and there's no tenant-configurable policy to block arbitrary admin-defined topics (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/security-and-governance)

Prompts, responses and data accessed through Microsoft Graph aren't used to train foundation LLMs, and Copilot services opted out of Azure OpenAI abuse-monitoring human review (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/microsoft-365-copilot-privacy)
Copilot use is covered by the Microsoft DPA and Product Terms with Microsoft as processor ('enterprise data protection') (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/enterprise-data-protection)

Bing web grounding queries leave the Microsoft 365 boundary: they strip user and tenant IDs, fall under the Microsoft Services Agreement with Microsoft as an independent controller, and are outside the EU Data Boundary and outside HIPAA/BAA coverage (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/enterprise-data-protection)

Copilot is an EUDB service and EU traffic stays in the EUDB, with exceptions (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/microsoft-365-copilot-privacy ; https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/enterprise-data-protection)

Anthropic Claude models used as a subprocessor in Microsoft 365 Copilot are excluded from the EUDB and in-country processing commitments (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/microsoft-365-copilot-privacy ; https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/enterprise-data-protection)

OpenAI models are also offered as a subprocessor in Microsoft 365 Copilot, and admins decide whether to enable third-party models (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/microsoft-365-copilot-privacy)

Microsoft 365 Copilot became a covered workload in the Product Terms data residency commitments, Advanced Data Residency and Multi-Geo on 2024-03-01 (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/microsoft-365-copilot-privacy)
Non-EU customers' Copilot queries can be processed in the US, EU or other regions (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/microsoft-365-copilot-privacy)

A Copilot Studio tenant with an EU or EFTA billing address is in EUDB scope only if all its environments are in EUDB regions, and generative AI features can be configured to move data across regions, for example when capacity is constrained (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/geo-data-residency)

Copilot audit events are on by default in Purview Audit (Standard): RecordType `CopilotInteraction` covers Microsoft Copilots, Cowork and Copilot Studio apps (AppIdentity `Copilot.Studio.<appId>`) (https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-copilot)

Copilot audit records include `AgentId` (for example `CopilotStudio.Declarative.<guid>`), `AccessedResources` with sensitivity labels, `XPIADetected`, `JailbreakDetected` and model provider/name (https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-copilot)

`AIAppInteraction`, and some `ConnectedAIAppInteraction` records, need Purview pay-as-you-go enabled and are kept 180 days; Copilot Studio agents on non-Microsoft channels also need Purview pay-as-you-go (https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-copilot ; https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/ai-copilot-studio)
DSPM for AI (classic) has been replaced by a new Purview DSPM, and the classic version is no longer enhanced (https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dspm-for-ai)

DSPM for AI provides one-click policies, weekly oversharing assessments of the top 100 SharePoint sites and activity explorer for Copilot and agent prompts (https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dspm-for-ai)
DSPM for AI needs a role such as Entra Compliance Administrator, plus Content Explorer Content Viewer to read prompt text (https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dspm-for-ai)

Sensitivity labels apply to Copilot and Copilot Studio agents, and encrypted labels require the `EXTRACT` and `VIEW` usage rights (https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/ai-copilot-studio ; https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/microsoft-365-copilot-privacy)

A DLP policy scoped to the Microsoft 365 Copilot location can stop Copilot and SharePoint-grounded Copilot Studio agents processing labelled content; retention uses the 'Microsoft Copilot Experiences' location (https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/ai-copilot-studio ; https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/microsoft-365-copilot-privacy)

Compliance attestations listed for Copilot (names only): GDPR, EU Data Boundary, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27018, HIPAA (properly configured, excluding web queries) and ISO/IEC 42001 (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/microsoft-365-copilot-privacy)

facts.fact: Copilot Chat has no extra cost and comes with eligible Microsoft 365 subscriptions, but agents and connectors to work data are metered (shown 2026-11-14) (https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-copilot/pricing/enterprise)

Microsoft 365 Copilot is $30/user/month paid yearly (shown 2026-11-14) and includes Work IQ grounding, Copilot in the Office apps and Teams, prebuilt agents (Researcher, Analyst, Facilitator) and SharePoint Advanced Management (https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-copilot/pricing/enterprise)

Copilot Business pricing is unconfirmed: third-party sources cite $21/user/month list price and an $18 promo with conflicting end dates, not confirmed on a Microsoft page (secondary) (https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/t5/microsoft-365-copilot-blog/act-now-lock-in-current-pricing-on-microsoft-365-copilot/ba-p/4502628)

Microsoft 365 E7 'Frontier Suite' is $99/user/month with annual commitment, and E7 (No Teams) is $90.45 (shown 2026-11-14) (https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365 ; https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoft_365blog/microsoft-365-e7-and-agent-365-are-now-generally-available/4516295)
Microsoft 365 E7 has been GA since 2026-05-01 (https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoft_365blog/microsoft-365-e7-and-agent-365-are-now-generally-available/4516295)
E7 bundles Microsoft 365 E5, Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Entra Suite and Microsoft Agent 365 (https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365)
Microsoft Entra Suite is bundled into Microsoft 365 E7 (https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365)

Microsoft Agent 365 is $15/user/month standalone with annual commitment (shown 2026-11-14), licensed per human user who interacts with, owns, manages or sponsors agents, not per agent, and isn't included in E3 or E5 (https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365 ; https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365/overview)
Microsoft Agent 365 has been GA since 2026-05-01 (https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365)
Copilot Credits replaced 'messages' on 2025-09-01 with no change to pack quantity or pay-as-you-go rate (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/billing-licensing)

Copilot Credits are the common consumption unit covering Copilot Studio agents, Copilot Chat agents for unlicensed users, Copilot Cowork and the Work IQ API (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/billing-licensing ; https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-copilot/extensibility/cost-considerations)
The Work IQ API is metered in Copilot Credits (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-copilot/extensibility/cost-considerations)

A prepaid Copilot Credit pack is $200/month for 25,000 credits, billed annually, with no rollover; pay-as-you-go is $0.01 per credit through an Azure subscription, billed in arrears (shown 2026-11-14) (https://www.microsoft.com/licensing/guidance/Microsoft-Copilot-Studio)

The Copilot Credit Pre-Purchase Plan (P3) is a one-year prepayment where 1 Copilot Credit Commit Unit (CCCU) = $1 = 100 credits, with tiers from 3,000 CCCUs for $2,850 (5% off) to 3,000,000 CCCUs for $2,400,000 (20% off), as shown 2026-11-14 (https://www.microsoft.com/licensing/guidance/Microsoft-Copilot-Studio)

Microsoft Agent Pre-Purchase Plan: 1 Agent Commit Unit (ACU) = $1, with tiers of 20,000 ACUs for $19,000, 100,000 for $90,000 and 500,000 for $425,000 (shown 2026-11-14) (https://www.microsoft.com/licensing/guidance/Microsoft-Copilot-Studio)
Agent Commit Units are usable for Copilot Credits or Microsoft Foundry (https://www.microsoft.com/licensing/guidance/Microsoft-Copilot-Studio)

Standard-harness billing rates: classic answer 1 credit, generative answer 2, agent action 5 (computer use is billed at this rate), tenant Graph grounding 10, agent flow actions 13 per 100 actions; reasoning models add 10 credits per 1,000 billed tokens with prompt-cache reads free; voice is 10, 35 or 75 credits per minute (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-messages-management)

Microsoft 365 Copilot license holders aren't charged credits for classic or generative answers and tenant Graph grounding in Copilot Chat, Teams or SharePoint when the agent runs as the licensed user; exceptions are computer-using agents, autonomous or event-triggered runs, and agent flows not started by 'When an agent calls the flow', and fair-use limits apply (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-messages-management ; https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/billing-licensing)

Microsoft Copilot harness agents bill from build time, not publish time: credits are charged for LLM tokens, tools (knowledge, MCP) and the harness itself, including natural-language authoring, testing and evaluations (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/billing-credit-overview)

Standard-harness agents start billing after publish, unlike Microsoft Copilot harness agents which bill from build time (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/billing-credit-overview)

Copilot Studio blocks an environment's agents, including mid-conversation, when the tenant reaches 125% of prepaid capacity, unless the environment has its own remaining allocation or a pay-as-you-go billing plan; agent flows are blocked separately once no credits remain (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-messages-management)

For Copilot Chat users without a Copilot license, instruction-only and public-web-grounded agents are free, while agents grounded in shared tenant data (SharePoint, Copilot connectors) consume Copilot Credits (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-copilot/extensibility/cost-considerations)
Microsoft 365 Copilot APIs are currently available only to Copilot-licensed users (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-copilot/extensibility/cost-considerations)

facts.fact: Usage-based Copilot Credits billing is set up in Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management, where admins create spending policies (identity-based or resource-based for Copilot Studio environments) with per-policy and per-user limits (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-setup)

Copilot Credits billing order is prepaid capacity packs, then P3, then pay-as-you-go (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-setup ; https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-monitor-spending)

Prepaid credits allocated to Power Platform environments reduce what's available to Microsoft 365 admin center services (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-monitor-spending)

An older Copilot pay-as-you-go flow still covers Copilot Chat, SharePoint agents and the Copilot Retrieval API (preview), linking billing policies to an Azure subscription; Cowork and Work IQ API use the newer Cost Management flow (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/pay-as-you-go-overview)
The older Copilot pay-as-you-go flow is managed by Global, Billing or AI Administrator (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/pay-as-you-go-overview)
Power Apps Premium is $20/user/month paid yearly, or $12 at a 2,000-seat minimum (shown 2026-11-14) (https://www.microsoft.com/power-platform/products/power-apps/pricing)
The Dataverse database capacity add-on is $40/GB/month (shown 2026-11-14) (https://www.microsoft.com/power-platform/products/power-apps/pricing)
Power Apps per app is no longer sold to new customers through some channels since 2026-01-02 (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/pricing-billing-skus)

Power Automate Premium is per user with 40k actions/day, one attended RPA bot, premium and custom connectors, process mining and 5,000 AI Builder credits/month (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/power-automate-licensing/types)

Power Automate Process is capacity assigned to a solution-aware cloud flow or a machine, with 250k actions/day and one unattended bot (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/power-automate-licensing/types)
Power Automate Hosted Process adds one Microsoft-hosted machine bot; Power Automate pay-as-you-go is also available (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/power-automate-licensing/types)

Microsoft 365 seeded Power Apps and Power Automate rights cover standard connectors only, not premium connectors, custom apps on Dataverse, premium flows or Copilot Studio agents; Power Automate cloud flows use Power Automate licensing, not Copilot Credits (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/pricing-billing-skus ; https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-messages-management)

Power Platform pay-as-you-go links an environment to an Azure subscription via a billing policy in Power Platform admin center that meters Power Apps, Power Automate, Dataverse, Power Pages and Copilot Studio usage (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/pricing-billing-skus)

Pricing pages are https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-copilot/pricing/enterprise, https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365, https://www.microsoft.com/licensing/guidance/Microsoft-Copilot-Studio and https://www.microsoft.com/power-platform/products/power-apps/pricing, and Microsoft's Copilot Studio Licensing Guide is at https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2320995 (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/billing-licensing)
